title: std/image-study@1
description: A handful of frames from one imaging study, with what is already known about it. Frames travel IN the envelope rather than by address, unlike std/media-asset@1, and the reason is the opposite of that schema's: these are pixels of a named person, and an address would mean whoever fetches them holds a credential to the archive. A reader is given a sample -- eight or sixteen frames, not the twelve hundred a CT has -- so an envelope stays a message. `deidentified` is a statement by the sender, not something this schema can verify: an ultrasound carries the patient's name burned into the pixels, and masking it is the sender's job.

frames.description: The sample, in the order a reader should see it.

mime.description: Rendered, not raw DICOM: a reader looks at what a person would look at, windowed the way the archive rendered it.

instance_uid.description: SOPInstanceUID, so a finding can name the image it is on rather than a position in this array.

frame.description: Frame number within the instance, for a multi-frame image.

deidentified.description: That the sender removed the identifiers -- the DICOM tags AND anything burned into the pixels. A reader refuses when this is false: it cannot check, and being the place where nobody checked is worse than refusing.

modality.description: DICOM modality of the study: CT, MR, US, CR, MG.

report.description: The report already on file, when there is one. A reader is asked to correlate with it and to say where it disagrees -- not to repeat it.

question.description: What the clinician is asking. Empty means a general read.

prior.description: The report of an earlier study of the same person, for comparison.
